methodologyNotes: Covers 12 current-generation (2025-2026 model year) full-suspension trail mountain bikes that buyers actively cross-shop in 2026: eight of the ten seed models (Trek Fuel EX 8, Specialized Stumpjumper, Santa Cruz Hightower, Canyon Spectral, Yeti SB-series, Cannondale Habit, Ibis Ripmo, Norco Sight) plus three additions for buyer-relevant breadth (Orbea Occam SL, Trek Top Fuel, Commencal Meta TR). Giant Trance X (seed) is included with a null price. Marin Rift Zone (seed) and four other candidates researched (Pivot Trail 429, Scott Spark, Rocky Mountain Instinct, Transition Sentinel) were DROPPED from the final set: marinbikes.com and every current-generation Rift Zone retailer listing found returned persistent HTTP 429 to automated fetches throughout this research pass, and the only in-stock Rift Zone data reachable was a four-year-old 2022 27.5 model — not a reliable current source — so nothing was published rather than risk stale/unverifiable data; the other four brands' storefronts (Shopify-hosted in every case) returned the same persistent 429/403 block and no independent current-year spec sheet could be assembled. Yeti's SB130 was discontinued; Yeti's own lineup refresh explicitly replaced it with the SB140, which is used here as the closest current equivalent (noted per-product). priceUsd is the lowest independently verified US MSRP for a complete bike in each model's current lineup; where the single cheapest build's own component spec sheet could not be confirmed (Orbea Occam SL's ~$2,999 H30 alloy tier was reported by press but its parts spec was unverifiable), the next fully-verified tier is priced instead and this is called out in priceNote. Several manufacturer storefronts (Trek, Specialized, Santa Cruz, Giant's build-specific pages) are JS-rendered or blocked automated fetches outright in this research pass; for those, authorized-dealer listings (chiefly BikeExchange, whose per-product pages mirror the brand's own PIM data and imagery) or independent press (BikeRadar, The Loam Wolf, Bikerumor, Wheat Ridge Cyclery) were used as primary/corroborating sources instead, with the access limitation noted per-product in provenance. weight_lbs is the manufacturer- or reviewer-claimed complete-bike weight for the exact priced build, converted from kg to lb (x2.20462) when the source only published metric; left null when no weight was published for that specific build. suspension_type records the manufacturer's own named linkage/platform (VPP, DW-Link, Maestro, ABP, Switch Infinity, Horst-link, Proportional Response, Contact System) exactly as published; left null where no linkage name was stated. groupset/drivetrain_speeds/brake_type reflect the exact priced build, not the top-of-range option. All prices and specs were checked against the cited source(s) on accessedAt 2026-08-01; no spec, price, or image was invented — unverifiable fields are null rather than guessed.

products.name: Trek Fuel EX 8 Gen 7
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,799.99 for the Fuel EX 8 Gen 7 (29", Alpha NEXT Platinum Aluminum, SRAM Eagle 70) per BikeExchange's Trek-dealer listing, which mirrors Trek's own product data and imagery.
products.provenance: trekbikes.com itself is JS-rendered and returned no usable product content to automated fetches in this research pass, so BikeExchange's live dealer listing for the "Trek Fuel EX 8 Gen 7 (29") 2026" was used as the primary source: Alpha NEXT Platinum Aluminum frame with internal storage and an adjustable leverage rate, 150mm Fox Rhythm 36 fork, ABP suspension, SRAM Eagle 70 12-speed (30T/10-52T), SRAM DB8 4-piston brakes, at $3,799.99 US MSRP. The Edge Cycleworks (UK retailer, GBP pricing) independently corroborates the identical spec sheet — same frame name, 150mm fork/145mm rear travel, SRAM Eagle 70 12-speed, SRAM DB8 brakes — and additionally states a manufacturer-claimed complete-bike weight of 16.89kg, converted here to 37.2lb. Both sources confirm this is the standard aluminum Fuel EX 8, not the carbon or XT variants.

products.name: Specialized Stumpjumper 15 Alloy
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,000, the stated starting price of the Stumpjumper 15 Alloy range, per BikeRadar's launch coverage citing Specialized's own pricing; this corresponds to the entry Shimano Deore build, whose full spec sheet is independently confirmed on BikeExchange's dealer listing for the identical "Shimano Deore Shadow - 140" configuration (sold out online, price not re-displayed there).
products.provenance: specialized.com returned HTTP 403 to every direct automated fetch in this research pass, so BikeRadar's editorial coverage of the Stumpjumper 15 Alloy launch (citing Specialized's own figures) was used as the primary source: M5 alloy frame with Trail Geometry, 145mm rear travel via Horst-linkage, a 150mm RockShox Psylo Silver fork on the entry alloy build, Shimano Deore drivetrain and Shimano BR-MT420 4-piston brakes on the base build, and a $3,000 starting US price. BikeExchange's dealer listing for the exact "Stumpjumper 15 Alloy (Shimano Deore Shadow - 140 - 29")" SKU independently corroborates every spec verbatim — Aluminium M5 Alloy chassis, 150mm RockShox Psylo Silver fork (the "140" in the dealer's SKU string denotes the build/rear-travel code, not fork travel — BikeRadar's launch coverage citing Specialized's figures confirms the entry alloy ships a 150mm fork, so fork_travel_mm was corrected from 140 to 150), 145mm rear travel via X-Fusion shock, Shimano Deore M6100 12-speed (10-51t), Shimano BR-MT420 4-piston brakes — and adds a manufacturer-claimed 16.57kg (36lb 8.5oz, converted to 36.53lb) weight not stated on the BikeRadar page. The two sources describe the same entry-tier Deore build, so the $3,000 base price is applied to this fully-specified configuration.

products.name: Santa Cruz Hightower 70
products.priceNote: US MSRP $5,149 for the 2026 Hightower 70 (Carbon C frame, SRAM 70 Eagle T-Type), the entry complete-bike build in Santa Cruz's six-tier 2026 Hightower range, per Wheat Ridge Cyclery's authorized-dealer listing.
products.provenance: santacruzbicycles.com returned HTTP 429 to every direct automated fetch attempt in this research pass, so Wheat Ridge Cyclery's authorized-dealer listing for the "Santa Cruz Hightower 70 - 2026" was used: 29" wheels, 160mm RockShox Lyrik Base fork, VPP suspension platform, SRAM 70 Eagle T-Type 12-speed mechanical (32t/10-52t), SRAM DB8 brakes with 200mm Centerline rotors, at $5,149.00 US price. Frame material (Carbon C) and the six-tier $4,999-$11,399 range were independently corroborated in prior search-engine-surfaced coverage citing Santa Cruz's own product data, matching this listing's $5,149 figure for the 70-tier build exactly. No manufacturer-claimed complete-bike weight was published on the fetched page, so weight_lbs is left null.

products.name: Canyon Spectral 6
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,099, Canyon's own listed price for the Spectral 6 (AL aluminum frame), the entry complete-bike tier of the current Spectral range, per Canyon's US product page.
products.provenance: Fetched Canyon's own US product page for the Spectral 6 directly (canyon.com/.../spectral-6/4012.html), which confirms: AL aluminum frame, 29" wheels with mullet (27.5" rear) option, 150mm Fox 36 Performance Elite fork, 140mm rear travel via a Fox Float X Performance shock, a Shimano SLX/Deore mixed 1x12 drivetrain (32T, 10-51t cassette), Shimano SLX 4-piston brakes with 203mm rotors, a manufacturer-claimed 34.09lb complete-bike weight (size M standard spec), and a $3,099 US price, listed as "Coming soon" at time of access. The page names the fork/shock brands and the frame's 64-degree head angle but does not name a specific suspension-linkage platform (e.g. Horst-link), so suspension_type is left null rather than assumed. No independent third-party retailer corroboration was completed for this specific 2025 Spectral 6 build within this research pass; all figures come directly from Canyon's own manufacturer page.

products.name: Yeti SB140 C2 90 Transmission
products.priceNote: US MSRP $6,200 for the 2026 SB140 C2 90 Transmission, the lowest-priced complete-bike build in Yeti's current SB140 range, per Yeti's own US product page. NOTE: this product replaces the requested seed "Yeti SB130" — Yeti discontinued the SB130 and its own current lineup positions the SB140 as its direct successor (confirmed via independent press coverage of Yeti's SB-family refresh).
products.provenance: The Yeti SB130 was discontinued; independent press coverage of Yeti's SB-family refresh (Pinkbike, The Loam Wolf, Blister) confirms the SB140 is Yeti's designated successor to the SB130, occupying the same short-travel trail slot in the current lineup, so it is used here as the closest verifiable current equivalent. Fetched yeticycles.com's own SB140 product page directly, which lists the 2026 build range and confirms the C2 90 Transmission — a C-Series carbon frame, 140mm rear travel via Switch Infinity suspension, 29" wheels, mechanical SRAM Eagle 90 T-Type drivetrain, and SRAM Maven Base brakes — as the lowest-priced complete bike at $6,200, with a 160mm-travel Fox Performance 36 fork per this build tier (verified against yeticycles.com's own build spec on accessedAt; an earlier draft's 150mm figure was a stale carry-over from the previous-generation SB140 and has been corrected). No manufacturer-claimed weight was found for this specific build during the research pass (airparkbikeco.com and vitalmtb.com, tried as independent corroboration, returned HTTP 429 and an unrenderable JS page respectively), so weight_lbs and independent corroboration are left absent rather than guessed.

products.name: Cannondale Habit 3
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,325 for the Habit 3 (29", SmartForm C1 Alloy, SRAM NX Eagle), Cannondale's entry complete-bike tier for its current Habit platform, per BikeExchange's dealer listing (shown discounted to $1,999.99, with the $3,325 MSRP stated).

specs.brake_type: SRAM G2 R hydraulic disc, 180/180mm rotors

products.provenance: Cannondale's family-overview page for the Habit is JS-rendered and returned no build/price data to automated fetches, but the individual Habit 3 product page (model code C23301U) loaded directly and confirms: SmartForm C1 Alloy frame at 130mm travel, 140mm RockShox Pike fork, RockShox Deluxe Select+ DebonAir rear shock, SRAM NX Eagle 12-speed (30T/10-50t), SRAM G2 R brakes with 180/180mm CenterLine rotors, and Cannondale's own "Proportional Response Suspension" naming — but no price (listed "Out of Stock Online"). BikeExchange's dealer listing for the identical "Habit 3 (29") 2023" SKU independently corroborates every spec verbatim and additionally states the $3,325.00 MSRP (discounted to $1,999.99 at the dealer). The model code and generation are unchanged since 2023 and this remains Cannondale's current-catalog entry Habit build as of this research pass.

products.name: Ibis Ripmo V3 (Deore)
products.priceNote: US MSRP $5,999 for the Ripmo V3 Deore build, the entry complete-bike tier of Ibis's current Ripmo (V3) lineup, per Ibis's own US product page and independently matched exactly by BikeExchange's dealer listing for the identical 2026 build.
products.provenance: Fetched ibiscycles.com's own Ripmo product page directly, which confirms a full-carbon front and rear triangle, a flip-chip 29"/MX wheel setup, 160mm fork travel, 150mm rear travel via DW-Link suspension, and a $5,999 starting price for the Deore build (frame weight 7.6lb, complete bike starting ~31.11lb). BikeExchange's dealer listing for "Ripmo V3 Deore Fox Factory 2026" independently corroborates the identical price ($5,999.00) and adds the exact build kit: Shimano Deore M6100 12-speed drivetrain (10-51t) and Shimano Deore M6120 4-piston brakes with 200/200mm RT66 rotors. Both sources confirm this is the current V3 generation, not the discontinued alloy "Ripmo AF" model.

products.name: Norco Sight A3 MX
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,499 for the Sight A3 MX, Norco's entry aluminum complete-bike tier for the current Sight platform, per BikeExchange's dealer listing (shown discounted to $2,599.00, with the $3,499 MSRP stated).
products.provenance: norco.com returned "Page Not Found" to every guessed product-page URL and defaulted to a French-Canadian locale on repeated automated fetches in this research pass, so BikeExchange's dealer listing for the "2025 Sight A3 MX" was used as the sole source: aluminum frame with Norco's High Pivot Horst suspension at 150mm travel, a 160mm RockShox fork, mixed 29"/27.5" (MX) wheels, RockShox Deluxe Select+ Air shock, Shimano Deore 12-speed drivetrain, Shimano Deore MT520 4-piston brakes (203mm front/180mm rear rotors), and a $3,499.00 US MSRP (discounted to $2,599.00 at the dealer). No manufacturer-claimed weight was listed, and no independent second source could be reached for this specific 2025 build within this research pass, so weight_lbs is left null and corroboration is omitted rather than fabricated.

products.name: Orbea Occam SL M30 (Alloy)
products.priceNote: US price $4,723.95 for the 2026 Occam SL M30 (Alloy) build per BikeExchange's dealer listing. Press coverage of the 2026 Occam SL launch (Bikerumor) cites a lower ~$2,999 starting price for the base alloy "H30" tier, but that specific tier's component spec sheet could not be independently verified in this research pass, so the fully-verified M30 Alloy configuration is documented here instead and the cheaper tier is noted for context.
products.provenance: orbea.com returned HTTP 403 to direct automated fetches in this research pass, so BikeExchange's dealer listing for the "OCCAM SL M30 (Alloy) 2026" was used as the primary source: aluminum frame, 29" wheels, Shimano 12-speed drivetrain (SLX shifter/XT derailleur, CS-M7100 10-51t cassette), Shimano M6100 hydraulic disc brakes, a Fox Float Performance rear shock, at $4,723.95 US price — but fork travel was not stated on this page. Bikerumor's coverage of Orbea's 2026 Occam SL/LT update independently confirms the Occam SL platform runs "140mm of travel front and rear" (corroborated further by Blister Review and Orbea's own "140mm Front and Rear Travel" tagline surfaced in the same research pass) and states pricing for both the ~$2,999 H30 alloy entry build and the ~$4,499-$4,794 M30 tier, consistent with the BikeExchange figure for the M30 Alloy. Orbea does not publicly brand a specific suspension-linkage name for the Occam platform in either fetched source, so suspension_type is left null rather than guessed.

products.name: Trek Top Fuel 5 Gen 4
products.priceNote: US MSRP $2,899 for the Top Fuel 5 Gen 4 (29", alloy frame, Shimano Deore), Trek's entry complete-bike tier for the Top Fuel platform, per BikeExchange's dealer listing (discounted to $2,299.99, with the $2,899 MSRP stated) and independently confirmed as the platform's entry price ("entry-level models starting at $2,899") in The Loam Wolf's long-term review of the Top Fuel Gen 4.
products.provenance: trekbikes.com's own Top Fuel 5 Gen 4 page is JS-rendered and did not expose its spec table to automated fetching, so BikeExchange's dealer listing was used as the primary source: alloy frame, 29" wheels, a 130mm RockShox fork, Shimano Deore drivetrain, and disc brakes, at $2,899.00 MSRP (discounted to $2,299.99 at the dealer). The Loam Wolf's long-term review of the Top Fuel Gen 4 platform independently confirms the shared platform architecture — Alpha Platinum/Silver Aluminum frame, Trek's ABP suspension link, 120mm rear travel (expandable to 130mm), a 130mm-travel fork on base builds, and explicitly states "entry-level models starting at $2,899" — matching the BikeExchange price exactly. The exact 12-speed Deore cassette range and 180/180mm rotor sizing for this specific tier-5 build were additionally cross-checked against several independent retailer/spec-database listings (opticycles.com, bike-room.com) surfaced during research but not independently re-fetched as full pages, so brake rotor sizing is reported with that caveat; weight was not published for this specific alloy tier-5 build (only for the higher aluminum Top Fuel 9), so weight_lbs is left null.

products.name: Giant Trance X
products.priceNote: Giant does not publish consumer USD MSRP on its own US site (dealer-network pricing model — build/price pages are gated behind a JS bike-finder tool that returned no pricing to automated fetches). The only USD prices for a "Trance X" found during this research pass were for the discontinued carbon Advanced Pro trim at prior model years (2022/2024) — a different frame-material tier from this aluminum-frame entry — so price is left null rather than attributed incorrectly.
products.provenance: Fetched Giant's own US and global showcase pages for the (aluminum) Trance X directly. Both independently confirm: ALUXX SL-grade aluminum frame (6011 alloy) with an Advanced Forged Composite rocker arm and flip-chip geometry adjustment, 29" wheels (2.5" max tire, 27.5" rear mullet capable), a 150mm-travel fork paired with 140mm of active rear-wheel travel via Giant's Maestro four-bar suspension linkage, and Boost hub spacing. Neither page — nor any dealer-specific build page reachable in this research pass — exposed a build-level component spec (drivetrain, brakes) or a US dollar price for the specific alloy Trance X trim; Giant's build/price selector is JS-rendered and returned empty content to automated fetching, and the only priced "Trance X" listings found (BikeExchange, prior model years) were for the carbon Trance X Advanced Pro, a different frame tier that would misrepresent this product if used. Per the null-beats-a-guess rule, drivetrain_speeds, groupset, brake_type, weight_lbs, releaseDate, and priceUsd are all left null, and no image is included since the only images found for a "Trance X" were confirmed to depict the different carbon Advanced Pro trim.

products.name: Commencal Meta TR V4 Origin
products.priceNote: US MSRP $2,800 for the Meta TR V4 Origin, Commencal's entry complete-bike tier for its current (V4) Meta TR trail platform, shown directly on Commencal's US direct-to-consumer site at a discounted $1,990.00 with the $2,800.00 MSRP stated.
products.provenance: Fetched Commencal's own direct-to-consumer US product page for the Meta TR V4 Origin (Heritage Green) directly, which lists all ten current Meta TR V4 complete-bike builds ($1,990-$5,200) and confirms for this entry tier: AL 6066 T4/T6 triple-butted aluminum frame, 29" wheels, a 150mm RockShox 35 Silver R fork, 140mm rear travel via a RockShox Deluxe Select shock and Commencal's own 2-position adjustable "Contact System" suspension, SRAM SX Eagle 12-speed (32t/11-50t), SRAM Guide T 4-piston brakes with 200mm rotors, a manufacturer-claimed 15.8kg (34.83lb, size S without pedals) weight, and a $2,800.00 MSRP (discounted to $1,990.00 at time of access). The product code (22METATRO) indicates the V4 platform's original 2022 design generation, which remains Commencal's current-catalog Meta TR as of this research pass; no independent second source was fetched for this direct-to-consumer-only model, so corroboration is omitted rather than fabricated.
